newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: swiss probe historian denies conflict of interest.
newsitem.headline: swiss probe historian denies conflict of interest.

text.p: The head of a historians' commission charged with reviewing Swiss relations with Nazi Germany on Tuesday rejected Jewish charges that his work for a bank cultural foundation was a conflict of interest.

Historian Jean-Francois Bergier said he saw no conflict of interest because the Jubilaeum Stiftung foundation was independent of Union Bank of Switzerland, which created the cultural body in 1962 to mark its 100th anniversary.

"I already said in a written statement in March that I would not seek re-election to the foundation's board when my term expires in November," Bergier told Reuters. He has been one of eight executive board members since 1991.
"There is no conflict of interest because the foundation has a purely cultural purpose and because it has nothing to do with the bank except that the bank donated the original capital," he said.

UBS, the country's biggest bank, said the foundation was legally and financially independent. Using a capital stock granted by UBS, the foundation distributes one million Swiss francs ($700,000) a year to cultural causes in Switzerland.
In New York on Monday the World Jewish Congress called on Bergier to resign immediately from the foundation's board.

WJC vice president Kalman Sultanik said Bergier's position, for which he is paid 5,000 Swiss francs ($3,500) a year, represented a conflict of interest because the historians' commission has to look into the wartime dealings of Swiss banks including UBS.
"This is a grotesque conflict of interest. He should have withdrawn from the foundation when he was appointed to the historians' commission," Sultanik said.

Bergier's commission, which started work in March, is charged by the Swiss government with making a sweeping account of the flow of money, treasures and other assets from Holocaust victims as well as Nazis through neutral Switzerland before, during and after World War Two.
